name: Gletscherweg Kaunertal
kurzbeschreibung: Gletscherweg Kaunertal leads into the glacier forefield of Gepatschferner above 2,000 m: glacier striations, moraine stages, and climate history.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Gletscherweg Kaunertal is a fascinating alpine glaciological educational trail at the very end of the Kaunertal in the Tiroler Oberland. It opens up the impressive glacier forefield of the Gepatschferner—with around 16 square kilometers of ice surface, Austria's second-largest glacier and the largest single glacier in the Eastern Alps. Embedded in the high-alpine pristine landscape of the Ötztaler Alpen below the glaciated Weißseespitze (3,518 m), the trail illustrates the landscape-shaping primal power of ice and the visible consequences of climate change at an elevation between 1,900 and 2,200 meters.

Natural Phenomena & Stations

The themed trail was designed in collaboration with glaciologists from the University of Innsbruck. Starting from the historic Gepatschhaus (1,928 m) or the Fernergries parking lot, the circular route leads through the valley shaped by glacial retreat. Along the path, numbered information panels document historic glacier extents since the maximum stand of the Little Ice Age in 1856. Hikers traverse diverse vegetation and erosion zones: from old stone pine and larch stands to colorful alpine rose meadows and sparse pioneer vegetation on fresh moraine walls. A geological highlight is the Roten Felsen—enormous roche moutonnée domes of reddish gneiss polished smooth by flowing glacier ice, featuring distinct striations and glacial polishing grooves. Further up, views open onto rushing meltwater torrents, giant glacial potholes, and the massive tongue of the Gepatschferner. The circular hike covers roughly six kilometers with approximately 250 meters of elevation gain and requires about two and a half to three hours of pure walking time.

Visit & Getting There

The Gletscherweg Kaunertal is freely and openly accessible during the snow-free summer months from mid-June to mid-October (take note of weather-related restrictions in case of fresh snowfall or rockfall hazard). Access is via the toll road Kaunertaler Gletscherstraße (day toll for cars approx. €32.00; toll is discounted or included for holders of the regional guest card Summercard GOLD or with the purchase of a mountain railway ticket). Arrival by car: Inntal Autobahn A12 to the Oberinntal/Prutz exit, through Kaunertal via Feichten, and further along the high-alpine toll road to the Fernergries parking lot or the Gepatschhaus. By public transit: ÖBB train to Landeck-Zams station, then Postbus line 230 via Prutz and Feichten directly to the Gepatschhaus or Fernergries stop.

Tips

Due to the high-alpine terrain with stony moraine paths, boulders, and wooden footbridges, the hiking trail is not barrier-free and unsuitable for regular strollers; ankle-high hiking boots with profile soles and weatherproof clothing are essential. After the hike, a stop at the heritage-protected Gepatschhaus—Austria's oldest Alpine Club hut, built in 1873—is highly recommended for traditional Tyrolean hut cooking. In good weather, continuing along the glacier road to the Weißseeferner at 2,750 meters is well worth the trip.
